# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** 45  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Grafton  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Lavendar is a little lady with an almost girlish face, pink cheeks, sweet lips, dimples, and big, soft brown eyes. She has snow-white hair that is beautifully wavy, thick, and arranged in puffs and coils. She wears dainty gowns, such as cream muslin adorned with pale-hued roses, which suit her so well that her age feels irrelevant.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c27 P25](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0025), [v2 c27 P58](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0058), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029)_

## Personality

Miss Lavendar possesses a youthful, romantic imagination and enjoys "pretending" things, often treating life with lighthearted playfulness despite her age. She is open to defying dietary warnings and loves hostessing tea parties with rich treats. Admitting to a proud and sulky streak when younger, she nevertheless carries a resilient, happy spirit that enjoys simple pleasures like peanut candy, flowers, and dreams. She forms deep, intuitive friendships with kindred spirits and holds a wistful fear of losing people she loves.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)_

## Traits

- imaginative and fond of pretending  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003)</sub>

## Abilities

## History

Miss Lavendar lived at Echo Lodge in Grafton for many years in quiet seclusion after a youthful quarrel parted her from her fiancé, Stephen Irving. Because she could not afford grown servants after her mother passed away, she adopted a system of hiring young girls for board and clothes, calling each of them "Charlotta" to avoid confusion. In her mid-forties, she met Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, developing a warm friendship with Anne as a kindred spirit. Through Anne's introduction of young Paul Irving, Stephen Irving learned of Miss Lavendar's unmarried status and returned to court her. The two reconciled, leading to a simple wedding ceremony held in the honeysuckle arbor at Echo Lodge.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c28 P22](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0022), [v2 c29 P5](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0005), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because he loved the scent after sleeping in lavendar-scented sheets while visiting her mother's home  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Engaged twenty-five years ago to Stephen Irving  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- Quarreled with Stephen Irving out of pride and vanity, leading to their long separation  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Began hiring young handmaidens for board and clothes after her mother died ten years earlier, calling each one "Charlotta"  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> But what is the use of being an independent old maid if you can’t be silly when you want to, and when it doesn’t hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

> I was just as proud as he was . . . pride and sulkiness make a very bad combination, Anne. But I could never care for anybody else and I didn’t want to. I knew I would rather be an old maid for a thousand years than marry anybody who wasn’t Stephen Irving.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> A broken heart in real life isn’t half as dreadful as it is in books. It’s a good deal like a bad tooth . . . though you won’t think that a very romantic simile.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> Oh, sometimes, I think it is of no use to make friends. They only go out of your life after awhile and leave a hurt that is worse than the emptiness before they came.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>
